official.name: Standard Moroccan Amazigh (Tamazight)
official.note: official since 2011; written in the distinct Tifinagh script, seen on motorway signage since 2015

notable.name: French
notable.note: no official status but widely used in business/government/education; colonial-era legacy

language.script: Arabic script (Arabic) + Tifinagh script (Tamazight) + Latin (French) — road signs are frequently bilingual or trilingual, a genuinely distinctive three-script combination

terrainDescription.zh: 北部為地中海沿岸與里夫山脈，中央有中亞特拉斯與高亞特拉斯山脈縱貫，南部與東部逐漸過渡為撒哈拉沙漠。
terrainDescription.en: A Mediterranean coast and the Rif mountains in the north, the Middle and High Atlas ranges running through the center, transitioning to Sahara desert in the south and east.

plate.color: white background, black text (changed from dark-blue text under a 2019 decree to align with European/Maghreb practice)

roadInfra.bollardStyle: No distinctively documented national style found — not a confirmed clue

utilityPole.transformerMount: Not independently documented for Morocco specifically — flagging as unconfirmed rather than guessing a style

historicalContext.zh: 摩洛哥路牌常見阿拉伯語、法語、塔馬齊格特語（柏柏爾語）三語並列，塔馬齊格特語自2015年起在高速公路標誌上採用獨特的提非納字母（Tifinagh），是全世界少見在道路標誌上使用此文字系統的國家。
historicalContext.en: Moroccan road signs commonly appear in Arabic, French, and Tamazight (Berber) together; since 2015, Tamazight has used the distinctive Tifinagh script on motorway signage — one of the very few places in the world where this script appears on road infrastructure.
